label: TMUA.co.uk · Trigonometry · Degrees to radians

hints.title: Anchor the two units
hints.body: A half-turn measures 180∘ or π radians. Both numbers describe the same angle.
hints.recap: Use <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>180</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow></math> radians as the conversion anchor.
hints.pitfall: Degrees and radians are two units for an angle, not two different angles.
hints.pause: Write what fraction of a half-turn <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>120</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math> represents.

recall.reminder: Convert between degrees and radians using <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>180</mn><mrow><mo>∘</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow></math> radians.

hints.title: Choose the conversion direction
hints.body: To convert degrees to radians, multiply the number of degrees by π180. To convert radians to degrees, use 180π instead.
hints.recap: The conversion factor depends on the starting unit.
hints.pitfall: Multiplying by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>180</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> here converts in the wrong direction.
hints.pause: Apply the conversion factor to the supplied angle and reduce the numerical fraction.

recall.reminder: Check the direction of conversion before substituting into a trigonometric function.

hints.title: Check against a familiar angle
hints.body: 120∘ is between 90∘ and 180∘. Its radian measure must therefore lie between π2 and π.
hints.recap: Check a converted angle against quarter- and half-turn benchmarks.
hints.pitfall: The answer is an angle in radians, so dropping the factor <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow></math> changes its size.
hints.pause: Identify the option matching your simplified fraction of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow></math>.

recall.reminder: Use standard angles to check the scale of a converted input.

solution:
Since 180∘=π radians, 120∘=(120180)π=2π3 radians: A.

This lies between π2 and π, as expected. The reverse conversion multiplies a radian measure by 180π. When the angle is inside a function such as xsinx, convert that angle input only; an ordinary multiplier outside sine stays unchanged.
knowledgePattern: Convert degrees to radians using a half-turn anchor
fallbackReason: The official archive has one direct calculator-mode conversion question, used as the original here. This observed TMUA.co.uk exercise supplies direct degree/radian conversion practice before the two official angle-input transfer questions.
